draft.title: The empirical rule
card: In a normal distribution, scores cluster around the mean. The empirical rule says how much of the data lies within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations of the mean.
About 68% of scores lie within 1 standard deviation of the mean. About 95% lie within 2, and about 99.7% lie within 3.
The distribution is symmetric, so the percentages split evenly either side of the mean. Within 1 standard deviation, about 34% lie on each side.

Example: test marks have mean 60 and standard deviation 10. Within 2 standard deviations means 40 to 80, so about 95% of marks are in that range. The other 5% are split evenly, so about 2.5% score above 80.
draft.remember: Within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations of the mean: about 68%, 95% and 99.7%.

a.q: Heights of Year 12 students are normally distributed, with mean 170 cm and standard deviation 8 cm. About what percentage of heights lie between 154 cm and 186 cm?
a.why: 154 and 186 are each 16 cm from the mean, which is 2 standard deviations. About 95% of scores lie within 2 standard deviations. 68% is tempting, but that is the share within only 1 standard deviation, 162 to 178.
a.clue: Find how many standard deviations 154 is below the mean.

b.q: Bags of rice have a normal distribution of mass, with mean 1000 g and standard deviation 20 g. About what percentage of bags have a mass above 1040 g?
b.why: 1040 g is 2 standard deviations above the mean. About 95% of bags lie within 2 standard deviations, so about 5% lie outside, split evenly between the two ends. That gives 2.5% above 1040 g. 5% is wrong because it counts both ends.
b.clue: The scores outside the range are split evenly between both ends.
